draft.title: Communism and capitalism
card: After 1945 the Soviet Union and the United States ran their countries in very different ways. These differences were a main source of Cold War rivalry.
a one-party state run by the Communist Party, with no free choice between parties. The state owned most industry and farmland and used a central plan to set what was made.
a democracy where citizens voted in elections between competing parties. Most businesses were privately owned and prices were set mainly by the free market.
Each side saw the other's system as a threat to its own way of life. This made it hard to trust each other.
draft.remember: The Soviet Union had one party and a planned economy. The United States had elections and free markets.

a.q: Which feature belonged to the Soviet Union after 1945?
opts: A central plan set what factories made
Private owners set prices in free markets
Voters chose between several parties
Businesses competed to win customers
a.why: In the Soviet system the state owned most industry and a central plan decided output. The other options describe the free market and multiparty democracy of the United States.
a.clue: Think about who decided what factories made.

b.q: In 1950 a citizen can vote between two parties and open a private shop to compete with others. Which country is this most likely to be, and why?
opts: United States, as it had elections and private business
Soviet Union, as it had elections and private business
United States, as the state planned all production
Soviet Union, as the state allowed several parties
b.why: Choice between parties and privately owned businesses matched the United States. The Soviet Union allowed only one party and the state owned most industry, so the other options mix up the two systems.
b.clue: Match both the voting and the shop to one system.

a.best: A central plan set what factories made

b.best: United States, as it had elections and private business
